technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot REST controllers to implement the module upload REST API.
Store uploaded module artifacts in a configurable file system location (e.g., local directory or cloud storage).
Replace hard-coded module registry with a database-backed registry (e.g., using JPA and an embedded H2 database) that is updated upon upload.
For module migrations, create new Spring Cloud Stream binder modules following the existing conventions in the target repositories (s-c-s-m and s-c-s).
Use standard dependency management (Maven/Gradle) and reuse existing test frameworks (JUnit, Mockito, Spring Boot test).
assumptions: The developer has access to the existing Spring XD source code and can extract the modules.
The target repositories (spring-cloud-stream-modules and spring-cloud-stream) already contain the necessary build infrastructure and CI pipelines.
Each module migration involves copying, adapting to Spring Cloud Stream APIs, and adding tests; no major architectural redesign is required.
Effort estimates exclude code review, CI setup, and deployment tasks as they are pre-existing.
The developer is familiar with Spring Framework, Spring Cloud Stream, and Spring XD.
Testing includes unit tests and integration tests for each module and the upload feature.
